cards.explanation: The answer is True. The song says, “salvation is established as its walls and ramparts.” Walls made of salvation, friends. My bakery walls can't even hold a calendar straight. (Isaiah 26:1)

The answer is faithful. The song calls for the gates to be opened for a righteous nation, “…one that remains faithful.” Remains is the word that counts there, friends. That's the neighbor who actually returns your ladder, and everybody knows how rare that is. (Isaiah 26:2)

The answer is because he trusts in God. The song says God keeps the steadfast of mind in perfect peace, “…because he trusts in You.” The peace has a reason, friends, and the reason is trust. It's not about how quiet life happens to be. (Isaiah 26:3)

The answer is because He is the Rock eternal. The song says, “…GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.” My edges wore down, bakers, but a Rock eternal doesn't wear down at all. That's a reason worth leaning on. (Isaiah 26:4)

The answer is the oppressed. The song says the lofty city is trampled by “…the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.” The ones who were pushed down are the ones walking over it, friends. That's quite a turn. (Isaiah 26:6)

The answer is His name and renown. The singers say, “Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.” They aren't asking for a thing, friends. They want Him. Now that's a wish list worth having. (Isaiah 26:8)

The answer is that the people of the world learn righteousness. The song says, “…the people of the world learn righteousness.” When God's judgments come, the whole world gets a lesson, bakers. I only wish my cookie class went that well. (Isaiah 26:9)

The answer is False. The song says, “Though grace is shown to the wicked man, he does not learn righteousness.” Even with grace shown, he doesn't learn, friends. I'd call that a very full plate that never got touched. (Isaiah 26:10)

The answer is the majesty of the LORD. The song says the wicked man acts unjustly “…and fails to see the majesty of the LORD.” That's like walking through my bakery and not noticing the ovens are on, friends. (Isaiah 26:10)

The answer is zeal. The song says, “They will see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame.” Zeal means He cares fiercely about His people, friends. The verse says they do not see His upraised hand, but it says they will see His zeal. (Isaiah 26:11)

The answer is the LORD. The singers say, “…all that we have accomplished, You have done for us.” They look at their whole list and hand the credit straight to Him, friends. That's a good habit for any baker with a full cookie box. (Isaiah 26:12)

The answer is the LORD's name alone. The singers say, “…Your name alone do we confess.” Other lords have ruled over them, friends, and still they confess only His name. That's one name on the whole list. (Isaiah 26:13)

The answer is all the borders of the land. The song says, “You have extended all the borders of the land.” The singers say twice that He has enlarged the nation, and they say He extended the borders too, bakers. That's a lot of room to grow. (Isaiah 26:15)

The answer is a quiet prayer. The song says, “when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.” In their distress it came out soft, friends. You don't need a big voice for this kind of prayer. (Isaiah 26:16)
The answer is wind. The singers say, “…we gave birth to wind.” All that pain, and nothing solid at the end, friends. That's a rough picture, and I think they felt it. (Isaiah 26:18)
The answer is False. The song says, “Your dead will live; their bodies will rise.” They don't stay in the dust, friends. After all that wind, this is where the song turns. (Isaiah 26:19)
The answer is awake and sing. The song says, “Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!” Dust doesn't get the last word here, bakers. It's a wake-up call with a tune attached. (Isaiah 26:19)

The answer is a little while until the wrath has passed. The call says, “Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.” A little while, and then it's over, friends. The ending is built right into the instruction. (Isaiah 26:20)

The answer is punish. The song says the LORD is coming out of His dwelling “…to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity.” That's the reason to hide, friends. It's a serious verse, so I'll keep my mustache still for it. (Isaiah 26:21)

The answer is True. The song says, “The earth will reveal her bloodshed and will no longer conceal her slain.” I think this one is heavy, friends. The verse says the earth will no longer conceal her slain. (Isaiah 26:21)

The answer is slay. The song says, “…and He will slay the dragon of the sea.” Leviathan, the fleeing and coiling serpent, is the one the sword is aimed at, friends. This is where the passage ends. (Isaiah 27:1)
